title: Dynamic SKU Tiling and PPK Variance Exploration
content:
Purpose: exploratory workbook + narrative for a tiling-based SKU strategy that reduces per-request PPK (price-per-thousand-tokens) while preserving latency SLOs. This is a working spreadsheet style doc: mix of clear formulas, scenario notes, and TODOs. Not final; intended for review by product + infra + finance.

High-level thesis:
- Instead of one-size-per-model pricing and capacity, use dynamic SKU tiling: group requests by latency tolerance and sequence-length distribution into discrete SKU buckets.
- Combine tiling with cache-first fallbacks and opportunistic quantized model variants to reduce marginal COGS for long-tail usage.
- Simulate PPK and margin impact across regions given representative request shape samples.

Key spreadsheet tabs (quick guide):
1) Summary: top-level charts and recommended actions (see action items).
2) Raw assumptions: cost inputs, GPU/hour, amortization, regional power, network, storage.
3) Per-model-region grid: matrix of model family x region x quantization level with derived per-token marginal COGS.
4) Sim scenarios: Monte Carlo-ish scenarios for peak/steady/long-tail traffic and slot utilization assumptions.
5) Recommended tiling: SKU definitions, latency buckets, tile sizing, expected PPK, forecasted margin uplift.

Raw assumptions (excerpts):
- GPU amortized blended cost (us-west): $1.20 / GPU-hour for A100 reserved mix (includes hw capex + infra ops amortization).
- GPU amortized blended cost (eu-west): $1.40 / GPU-hour.
- Tokens per GPU-hour (baseline small-chat model, 8k context, no KV cache): 120M tokens/hr.
- Avg tokens per request (hosted API): 40 input + 80 output = 120 tokens.
- Network + infra overhead per token: $0.0000008.
- Storage/amortized model weights per token (hot): $0.00000015.
- Effective quantized speedup multipliers: int8 -> 1.55x tokens/hr, int4 -> 2.8x tokens/hr (model dependent).
- Prefix/KV cache hit saves 60% of per-request compute tokens (approx) when applicable.

Representative formula examples (to appear in sheet cells):
- tokens_per_gpu_hour_adj = base_tokens_per_gpu_hour * quant_mult * batching_efficiency
- gpu_compute_cogs_per_token = (gpu_hour_cost / tokens_per_gpu_hour_adj)
- total_cogs_per_token = gpu_compute_cogs_per_token + network_overhead + storage_per_token + infra_margin_buffer
- ppk = total_cogs_per_token * 1000
- expected_margin = retail_price_ppk - ppk

Per-model-region grid (illustrative rows):
- model: small-chat-v1 | region: us-west | quant: fp16 | tokens/hr: 120M | gpu_cogs/token: $0.00001 | total_cogs/token: $0.000012 | ppk: $0.012 | retail_ppk (current): $0.015 | margin_ppk: $0.003 (20%)
- model: small-chat-v1 | region: us-west | quant: int4 | tokens/hr: 336M | gpu_cogs/token: $0.0000043 | total_cogs/token: $0.0000074 | ppk: $0.0074 | retail_ppk: $0.015 | margin_ppk: $0.0076 (51%)
- model: long-form-v2 | region: eu-west | quant: fp16 | tokens/hr: 45M | gpu_cogs/token: $0.000031 | total_cogs/token: $0.000034 | ppk: $0.034 | retail_ppk: $0.06 | margin_ppk: $0.026 (43%)

Notes on batching and tiling multipliers:
- batching_efficiency modeled as 1 + 0.12 * log10(avg_batch_size) capped at 2.2 (empirical from runtime traces).
- tiling_effectiveness: small tiles (latency-sensitive) get lower batch sizes -> lower efficiency, but ticketed into premium SKU. Larger tiles (async/low-latency-tolerance) have high batch and cache reuse.

SKU tiling proposal (recommended config):
- SKU-A (latency gold): targets <=150ms tail; FIFO slots, no tiling. Expected retail_ppk: +30% markup vs base. Use fp16 or int8 for parity.
- SKU-B (balanced): targets 250-600ms tail; small tiling window (50ms) to permit micro-batches and prefix cache. Default for most PLG traffic.
- SKU-C (economy): targets >600ms acceptable; batch window 200ms, allow int4 quantized variants and model fallback to cheaper family when cold.

Fallback matrix (example): request arrives for model X in region Y -> policy: if backend slot wait > 120ms and request in SKU-B, route to SKU-C variant (quantized) unless request contains "must_preserve_formatting" metadata. Track quality delta via evaluation set (auto-regress check).

Sim scenarios & results summary (selected runs):
- Baseline (no tiling): blended PPK = $0.022; blended margin = 28%
- Tiling + cache (balanced adoption: 45% of requests go to SKU-B, 20% eligible for SKU-C): blended PPK = $0.0128; blended margin = 46%
- Aggressive quantization + tiling (60% SKU-C adoption): blended PPK = $0.0096; blended margin = 56% but quality risk increased for certain prompts (see risk matrix tab).

Quality & risk guardrails:
- Always run continuous eval set per model-family/quantization pair. Raise auto-rollout block if average rouge/semantic-sim drops > 2% vs baseline on coaching prompts.
- Implement sampling of SKU-C responses for human review (1:1000 ratio rolling) for first 4 weeks after changes.

Actionable recommendations (owner + priority):
- A1: Add telemetry events to capture per-request "latency-tolerance" hint and sequence-length bucket (owner: Miguel Rivera, ETA: 2025-03-10, priority: high).
- A2: Build small experiment routing rule for one low-risk customer segment to trial SKU-B tiling (owner: Asha Patel, ETA: 2025-03-20, priority: high).
- A3: Update pricing page + SKU naming draft for marketing review (owner: Laura Chen, ETA: 2025-03-25, priority: medium).
- A4: Quantization rollout plan for int4 variants with per-model quality gates and canary (owner: Samir Desai, ETA: 2025-04-05, priority: high).

Open questions / items to validate:
- Real-world batching distribution: our logs show heavy skew to single-request batches for conversational endpoints — how much can we increase batch sizes without violating tail SLOs? (tracing: infra/trace-logs-2025-02).
- Regional power price sensitivity: eu-west energy spike scenario increases blended PPK by ~18% — should we bias routing for long batch windows away from EU during peaks?
- Customer acceptance: do enterprise customers accept slower SKU-C for cost savings, or do they prefer reserved capacity? Survey suggested mixed appetite.

Appendix (spreadsheet formulas and naming conventions):
- Column names in Per-model-region grid: model_family | region | quant | tokens_per_gpu_hr | gpu_hour_cost | gpu_cogs_per_token | net_overhead_per_token | total_cogs_per_token | retail_ppk | margin_ppk | recommended_sku
- Example cell formula: =IF(B2="us-west",gpu_us_west_hourly/(tokens_base*quant_mult*batch_eff),gpu_eu_hourly/(tokens_base*quant_mult*batch_eff))

Revision history:
- 2025-02-12 Laura Chen created draft with base assumptions and initial grid.
- 2025-02-20 Miguel Rivera added batch efficiency model and telemetry notes.
- 2025-03-01 Samir Desai appended quantization rollout steps and updated sim results.

Quick ask for reviewers: please check the per-token overhead assumptions and the recommended tiling latency thresholds. If you have raw request-shape samples for 2024-Q4 (by region), attach them to linked artifacts so we can re-run sims with live distributions.
